title: High-Access Employees
summary: Given a 2D array of strings representing employee access times, identify employees who accessed the system three or more times within any one-hour period.
statement: Given a 2D array of strings representing employee access times, identify employees who accessed the system three or more times within any one-hour period. Access times are in a 24-hour format. Exclude times with exactly one hour between them and times at the start and end of the day. Return a list of high-access employee names in any order.
constraints: Each record contains a lowercase employee name and a same-day four-digit 24-hour time.
An employee qualifies after at least three accesses spanning strictly less than sixty minutes.
Do not wrap across midnight; return qualifying names in any order.
hints: After sorting one employee’s times, any qualifying group contains three consecutive accesses within the sorted list.
Convert times to minutes, group by name, and compare each time with the one two positions earlier.
Qualify when times[i]-times[i-2]<60 for any i.
If any three accesses fit, their earliest three consecutive representatives fit; conversely every detected triple directly witnesses the condition.
editorial: If any three accesses fit, their earliest three consecutive representatives fit; conversely every detected triple directly witnesses the condition.

tests.explanation: Employee a has three accesses from 05:32 through 06:21.
Both c and d have a three-access window shorter than one hour.
